page: Amazon Web Services is4gen.4xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor operating on the arm64 architecture at 2.5 GHz. The server provides 16 dedicated physical cores across 16 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, backed by 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 32 MB shared L3 cache. Memory provisioning sits at 96.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:6 core-to-memory ratio (6.0 GB per core). For network throughput, it features a 25 Gbps baseline connection. It carries zero GPU accelerators and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

A central component of the is4gen.4xlarge hardware profile is its high-density bundled local storage, featuring 15,000 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate steady multi-core execution alongside predictable high-capacity I/O behavior. The instance achieved 24,283.13 in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing, a PassMark CPU score of 9,809.75, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 61.45 GB/sec, placing it in the middle tier of comparable cloud hardware. In-memory operations yielded 19.11 million operations per second in Redis SET testing, complemented by a PassMark database operations metric of 10,360.89.

Hardware tradeoffs emerge primarily in single-threaded compute density and specialized processing. Single-core performance falls into lower tiers, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 946.0, single-threaded gzip compression at 20.28 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 7.36 GB/sec. The absence of AVX, AVX-512, and AMX instruction extensions limits heavy vector operations, while LLM inference benchmarks reflect low generation speeds on medium-to-large models. Additionally, the PassMark memory score of 1,810.8 is positioned in the bottom 25th percentile.

Relative to standard compute options, the is4gen.4xlarge prioritizes cost efficiency for storage-dense architectures requiring significant local low-latency NVMe volumes alongside balanced memory. It is appropriate for distributed file systems, high-capacity NoSQL and relational database nodes, large log aggregation clusters, real-time analytics pipelines, and data search indices that benefit from fast local storage and steady multi-threaded throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services is4gen.4xlarge is a storage-optimized, arm64-based cloud server powered by a 16-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Configured on the Nitro hypervisor, it integrates 96.0 GB of memory (a 1:6 vCPU-to-RAM ratio) and an integrated 15,000 GB local NVMe SSD array alongside a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no dedicated GPUs. In multi-threaded benchmarking, the instance reliably matches middle-tier performance thresholds, generating 24,283.13 on stress-ng multi-core and 19.11 million ops/sec on Redis SET benchmarks. However, single-threaded execution and intensive vector arithmetic exhibit measurable performance constraints due to lower single-core frequencies and the absence of AVX instruction extensions. The instance delivers solid qualitative cost efficiency for I/O-intensive architectures requiring dense local NVMe storage and balanced memory, such as distributed databases, log ingestion engines, real-time data streaming clusters, and analytical data stores.
